claims.text: The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr alloy is produced by vacuum arc melting.
Replacing half of the Hf content with Al gives the target composition Al0.5Hf0.5MoTaTiZr.
Using vacuum arc melting for the modified alloy will ensure a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
Al has sufficiently lower atomic weight than Hf to reduce the modified alloy's overall density.
Partial replacement of Hf by Al will not significantly disturb the lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening of HfMoTaTiZr.
Retaining Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr will preserve lattice distortion and electronic interactions essential for high yield strength.
Replacing half of the Hf with Al will avoid formation of detrimental secondary phases.
The 50% Hf-to-Al substitution will reduce density by approximately 10–15% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy's room-temperature yield strength will remain within approximately 10% of the 1600 MPa baseline.
The modified alloy will retain a room-temperature yield strength of at least approximately 1400 MPa.
The modified alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C will remain within approximately 10% of the 855 MPa baseline.
The modified alloy will retain a yield strength of at least approximately 770 MPa at 1000 °C.
Changes in phase stability and elemental interactions may reduce mechanical-property retention after Al substitution.

contradictions.description: A room-temperature strength of 1400 MPa is a 12.5% decrease from the stated 1600 MPa baseline, so it is not within 10% and would fail the stated rejection criterion. A 10% retention threshold would require at least 1440 MPa.
